themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage (8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average, +611%) and missing signs (6 complaints last week vs. 1.1 average, +433%) are spiking simultaneously this week on the Upper East Side, suggesting potential widespread infrastructure failure or recent weather/construction damage affecting pedestrian safety and traffic navigation.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.53, +611%)
Street Sign - Missing: 6 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.63, +433%)
Two distinct but related sign categories spiking in same 7-10 day window suggests common root cause
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent storms, construction, or vehicle collisions triggered the spike; interview DOT about repair timelines
Document specific street locations with missing/damaged signs and assess pedestrian/traffic safety risks

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Accumulation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints reached 7 THIS WEEK versus a 1.5 weekly average (+367%, z-score 4.92), marking the highest single-week spike in this category—a potential indicator of rodent infestation, disease outbreak, or sanitation system failure requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: Dead Animal complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.92, +367%)
This week's 7 complaints represent single largest weekly count in 90-day dataset
Spike is acute (concentrated in current week) rather than gradual trend, indicating emerging event
reporting_angles: Consult DSNY and NYC Health Department on whether they've identified animal disease, pest infestation, or environmental contamination in the district
Interview residents in high-complaint neighborhoods to understand what they're observing; obtain specific addresses from 311 data

themes_detail.label: Illegal Street Signage Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Posting complaints jumped to 6 last week versus 0.6 weekly average (+860%, z-score 7.72), suggesting coordinated unauthorized advertising, political campaign activity, or loss of enforcement capacity—requires urgent verification of cause and scope.
evidence: Illegal Posting: 6 complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.72, +860%)
Spike is recent (last week) and represents 10x normal weekly volume
Related to Street Sign - Damaged/Missing spikes this week, suggesting broader street-level infrastructure/signage issues
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether illegal postings are concentrated in specific neighborhoods or corridors (suggest political campaign, commercial, or graffiti outbreak)
Contact DOE Enforcement to understand response time and whether staffing/resources are adequate to address spike

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Tree Damage complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK versus 0.9 weekly average (+357%, z-score 5.21), indicating potential organized or environmental tree destruction that threatens the district's canopy and requires investigation into cause (weather, development, vandalism).
evidence: Illegal Tree Damage: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.21, +357%)
Acute spike in current week suggests recent trigger (storm, construction, or intentional damage)
Tree damage aligns thematically with Street Sign Damaged/Missing and Dead Animal spikes, suggesting neighborhood-wide infrastructure disruption
reporting_angles: Identify specific tree locations from 311 complaints and determine whether damage is from storm, construction activity, or intentional vandalism
Interview Parks Dept on enforcement and whether this spike correlates with active development projects in the district (see 1904 recent DOB permits)

themes_detail.label: Helicopter Noise Sustained Anomaly
themes_detail.summary: Helicopter Noise complaints spiked to 11 three weeks ago (8700% above 0.1 weekly average, z-score 32.88)—the most extreme statistical outlier in the dataset—though timing is older; verify whether this is ongoing or resolved, as it represents a critical environmental/quality-of-life issue if sustained.
evidence: Helicopter Noise: 11 complaints three weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 32.88, +8700%)
Largest z-score spike in entire dataset, indicating unprecedented resident complaint volume for this category
Timeframe is 3 weeks old; recency lower than this-week spikes but severity and statistical power are exceptional
reporting_angles: Determine if spike was one-time event (e.g., presidential visit, emergency response) or ongoing condition; contact NYPD Aviation and FAA for flight logs
If ongoing, interview residents in high-complaint zones about quality-of-life impact and advocacy opportunities
